issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff may not unconditionally withdraw a suit during an appeal from a decree when doing so would destroy or prejudice rights vested under the decree, unless strong reasons show that the withdrawal will not affect or prejudice those rights.
material_facts: The trial court decreed the suit and declared the plaintiff owner of the disputed property.
After the decree, the plaintiff transferred the property to the appellants, who were impleaded as respondents in the pending appeal.
While the appeal was pending, the plaintiff sought to withdraw the suit after settling with one of the defendants.
Allowing withdrawal would have nullified the decree and prejudiced the transferees’ interests derived from it.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have allowed withdrawal. The withdrawal application was rejected, and the appeal was remanded for decision on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Order 23 Rule 1(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure gives a plaintiff a general right to withdraw a suit before a decree, subject to the restriction on bringing a fresh suit without leave under Rule 1(3). A decree under Section 2(2) conclusively determines the rights of the parties; once rights have vested under it, withdrawal during an appeal cannot be allowed as a matter of course if it would destroy or prejudice those rights. Withdrawal may be permitted only in rare cases where strong reasons show that no vested right will be affected or prejudiced. Hulas Rai Baij Nath v. K.P. Bass & Co. concerned withdrawal before a decree and did not decide the post-decree situation. The Court relied on the consistent approach in Tukaram Mahadu Tandel, Dharma Raja, Kedar Nath, Vidhydhar Dube, Kanhaiya, Thakur Balaram Singh, Ram Dhan, Guru Maharaj Anahdpur Ashram Trust, and Jutha Ram.

rule.if: appeal_from_trial_decree and plaintiff_seeks_withdrawal_during_appeal and decree_conclusively_determined_rights and withdrawal_would_prejudice_vested_rights and not strong_reasons_showing_no_prejudice

predicates.appeal_from_trial_decree: A party challenged a trial court decree in an appeal.
predicates.plaintiff_seeks_withdrawal_during_appeal: The plaintiff sought to withdraw the suit while the appeal was pending.
predicates.decree_conclusively_determined_rights: The decree conclusively determined rights in controversy in the suit.
predicates.withdrawal_would_prejudice_vested_rights: Allowing withdrawal would destroy or prejudice rights acquired under the decree.
predicates.strong_reasons_showing_no_prejudice: The plaintiff established strong reasons showing that withdrawal would not affect or prejudice any vested right.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks withdrawal during an appeal from a decree that conclusively determined rights, and withdrawal would prejudice vested rights without strong reasons showing otherwise, the withdrawal must be refused.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee who has been impleaded in an appeal concerning property transferred after a decree has a right to be heard before the plaintiff’s withdrawal of the suit is allowed if withdrawal would impair the transferee’s interest.
material_facts: The plaintiff transferred the property to the appellants after obtaining a decree declaring him its owner.
The appellants were impleaded as respondents in the appeal on the basis of the transfer.
The plaintiff later sought to withdraw the suit following a compromise with a defendant, which would have destroyed the decree on which the appellants’ interest rested.
The respondents alleged that the transfer deed was fraudulent, but the Court did not decide its legality.
issues.conclusion: The appellants had a right to be heard on the withdrawal application. The Court did not determine the validity of the transfer deed.
issues.legal_principle: Order 22 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits a person to be impleaded following a transfer of interest during litigation. Order 23 Rule 1-A addresses an application by a defendant to be transposed as a plaintiff when a suit is withdrawn or abandoned and requires consideration of whether the applicant has a substantial question against another defendant. Although the appellants had not applied for transposition, the Court held that their impleadment as transferees and the interest acquired after the decree gave them a right to be heard on withdrawal; they were virtually in the position of plaintiffs. The Court did not adjudicate the alleged fraud or the validity of the transfer.

predicates.appeal_from_trial_decree: A party challenged a trial court decree in an appeal.
predicates.transferee_acquired_interest_after_favor: A person acquired an interest in the disputed subject matter from the decree-favoured party after the decree was made.
predicates.transferee_was_impleaded_in_appeal: The transferee was added as a party to the pending appeal on the basis of the transfer.
predicates.withdrawal_would_impair_transferee_inter: Allowing withdrawal would destroy or impair the interest the transferee acquired in reliance on the decree.

issues.definition: If a transferee acquired an interest after a favorable decree, was impleaded in the appeal, and withdrawal would impair that interest, the transferee has a right to be heard on withdrawal.
